verdict.rationale: Supabase documents first-party background automation primitives. Cron schedules recurring jobs from every second to yearly that run SQL or invoke Edge Functions. Queues provides durable background tasks with guaranteed delivery, and Database Webhooks fire on table events. The MCP docs explicitly cover unattended agent routines, with pre-approved read-only tools and PAT-based CI access, and agents can deploy Edge Functions and run SQL to set these automations up. Missing for 10: hands-on or independent corroboration that cron/queue automations run reliably; a first-party agent-native scheduled runner (agent automations must be assembled from cron plus Edge Functions); fine-grained PAT scopes for unattended agents (all scopes currently required).
